title: Add structured output example using JSON Schema + runtime validation
author: Dana Lo
release_notes:
- TS SDK: add runnable structured output (JSON schema) example with validation + retry guidance
- Docs/README: clarify expected model support + common JSON pitfalls
description:
Context: We’ve had recurring confusion (and support tickets) around “structured output” examples that (a) don’t actually validate output, (b) assume JSON is always valid, and (c) don’t demonstrate what to do when the model returns invalid JSON. This PR adds a copy/paste runnable example for the TS SDK that requests schema-constrained JSON, validates it at runtime, and shows a safe fallback/retry pattern.

What’s included:
- New runnable example: structured output constrained by JSON Schema (strict), plus runtime validation of the parsed object.
- Uses AJV for JSON Schema validation (example-only dependency; no changes to SDK runtime behavior).
- README updates: how to run the example, required env vars, model notes, and a “known pitfalls” callout (invalid JSON, missing required fields, extra properties).

Why AJV:
- Matches our docs guidance (“JSON schema constraints + explicit validation”) and gives a realistic path for production code.
- Avoids the trap of “JSON.parse succeeded so we’re done”.

Notes / semantics:
- The example uses response_format=json_schema and strict=true.
- The example intentionally demonstrates defensive behavior: parse -> validate -> (if invalid) retry with a tighter system instruction and a max retry count.

Checklist:
- [x] Example runs end-to-end (Node 18+, pnpm)
- [x] Lint + typecheck
- [x] README steps verified
- [x] Links to support pitfall + docs terminology updated

Follow-ups (not in this PR):
- Add a small shared helper in examples/ for validation/retry patterns (kept local for now to minimize churn)
- Align docs-site code tab wording once redwood-docs PR-527 lands
